title: Boring but Big program review
summary: NH reviews Jim Wendler's Boring But Big 5/3/1 assistance template. He criticizes its static 5x10 back-off sets, which force sandbagging, add too much deadlift volume and risk overuse injuries, and its minimalist days that ignore many muscles. He prefers example 2's rotation of lifts but concludes it is a powerlifting program, not a hypertrophy one.
claims: Assistance templates that rotate, giving otherwise similar days different exercises and rep schemes, are a smart programming idea
After a heavy strength set like 5/3/1, back-off sets should evolve in volume and set count rather than stay static
5x10 is not a good rep scheme: many reps fall in submaximal intensity windows
A static 5x10 forces sandbagging because going to real failure on early sets would make sets 4-5 impossible
Boring But Big swings the pendulum from 5/3/1's too-low volume to too much volume at too little intensity
Back-off sets in the same style as the main lift can lead to overuse injury
Rep schemes need to be tied to specific lifts; you cannot swap a bench back-off scheme onto a close-grip bench
A day where only one lift gets taken to failure is picking favorites; strength work gives the best tonnage quality but not the majority, so other lifts must progress too
5x10 deadlifts after 5/3/1 is far too much volume; 50 deadlift reps at a relevant intensity will bury you
For deadlift back-off work, 3 sets of 3 is plenty
If you can do 50 deadlift reps and feel fine, the weight was too light to matter
Train abs every day for a strong core and defined abs, and fill the rest between ab sets with other small-muscle work
On a vertical press day, pair a vertical pull such as weighted pull-ups for 3 sets of 4-7 instead of 5x10 generic lat work
5x10 bench back-off sets will create shoulder problems; use close-grip bench 3x6-10 instead
On bench day, follow with a horizontal row for synergy
Proper fatigue across back-off sets should create a downward pyramid; keeping the same weight across 5x10 means you are sandbagging
In 5x10 squats and deadlifts many people will be limited by cardiovascular endurance, not muscular failure
Training squat and deadlift on the same day makes the second lift suffer
Opening with a horizontal press then following with a vertical press is NH's favorite way to program a bench day and good for shoulder health
Squats followed by deadlifts is a death combo: squat fatigue makes the thoracic spine round on deadlifts, and that loss of spinal integrity is when lower-back injuries happen
Two or three exercises per day is very low exercise selection and accumulating sets on them risks overuse injury
Two hip hinges on one day is worse for bodybuilding than pairing a knee-flexion movement with a hip hinge
Boring But Big lacks long-head triceps, rear delt, forearm, trap, calf, neck, biceps and superset ab work
Boring But Big is a powerlifting program, not a hypertrophy program; it will make you look like a powerlifter
NH does two horizontal presses a week even though he does not want too much chest hypertrophy; one per week is too little frequency for natural bodybuilding
exercises: better gains and safer for shoulders than 5x10 bench
better lat hypertrophy than 5x10 generic lat work
